title: Proactive SLO-driven trace sampler and exporter controller
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a control-plane component that watches latency and error SLO signals and proactively increases trace capture for affected services/endpoints, then restores baseline sampling when the SLO stabilizes. The controller should integrate with existing tracing hooks in the ingest path (trace-relay / trace-gateway) and with OTLP exporters to provide sampling hints and temporary high-fidelity export to Jaeger/Tempo backends. The goal is to ensure critical low-frequency errors and latency regressions are captured with sufficient trace context without permanently increasing export volume or storage costs.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can subscribe to SLO-derived alerts and Prometheus metrics (latency p95/p99, error-rate) and map them to service/endpoints in <1s after crossing threshold
When an SLO breach is detected, the controller raises sampling rate for targeted service/route to at least 50% (configurable) and signals relay via OTLP header/hint within 30s
Exports to Tempo/Jaeger for the elevated window increase only for affected keys and do not cause global export rate increases beyond configured safety limits
Console shows a live view of active SLO-driven sampling windows with start/end times, impacted routes, and expected token/cost delta
Automated rollback: controller automatically scales sampling back to baseline after configured quiet window (default 10m) or if cost threshold exceeded, with audit events emitted
E2E test harness demonstrates capturing an injected latency spike and subsequent increase in captured spans for the endpoint in the tempo test instance
Security review completed and design approved for header propagation and tenant isolation when modifying sampling hints
implementation_notes: Control loop lives in existing trace-relay service (lightweight mode) with feature flag to optionally run as separate controller service for scaling tests
SLO inputs: Prometheus rules + Alertmanager webhook + Console-derived SLO API. Normalize mapping to service:route identifier used by trace-relay
Propagation: use OTLP Resource/TraceTags or x-cloud-trace-sampling-hint header depending on downstream exporter; add mapping layer to translate to Jaeger/Tempo-compatible hint fields
Safety: per-tenant/global max-sampled-spans-per-minute limits; gradual ramp with token-bucket backpressure to avoid bursts to storage
Observability: emit metrics for controller decisions (windows opened/closed, samples raised, spans exported) and traces for decision flows for auditing
Rollout: start in internal staging with limit to non-prod tenants, then 10% prod canary, then full rollout tied to runtime-1.22 release
Cost model: estimate delta tokens for typical SLO window (based on past traffic) and surface estimated monthly cost impact in Console before enabling per-tenant
comments: 2026-02-10 Asha Patel: Initial ticket - proposal discussed with PM and Reliability. Agreed target: reduce time-to-detect/diagnose P95/P99 regressions by increasing trace fidelity around SLO violations.

2026-02-14 Liam Chen: Spike completed: prototype controller successfully toggled local relay sampling and produced additional traces in staging tempo instance. Observed 2.1x increases in exported spans for targeted endpoints.

2026-02-18 Sanjay Rao (SRE): Raised concern about burst exports causing downstream ingestion throttles. Proposed token-bucket global safety limit and per-backend queue monitoring. Added as implementation note.
2026-02-21 Priya Malhotra (PM): Request to surface expected cost delta in Console as part of enable flow. Added acceptance criteria and design doc link.
2026-02-24 Design review: agreed on OTLP header + Resource attribute dual-path for compatibility with both Jaeger and Tempo. Need security review for cross-tenant propagation paths.

2026-02-28 Liam Chen: Started integration work - created feature-branch and initial unit tests for mapping SLO -> service identifier. Linked draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-relay/pull/1423
test_plan: Run canary in staging with synthetic latency injections; verify metrics, exported spans count, and Console visualization. Add automated chaos test that flips SLO signals and validates controller behavior.
notes_for_reviewers: Key trade-offs: where to place the control loop (relay vs separate service), how aggressive pre-configured sample increases should be, and how to account for multi-tenant isolation and backend cost. Looking for review on safety limits and Console UI surface for per-tenant approvals.
